name: Heat Death gives Solar Eclipse's hit-chance debuff a 15 second duration (#930)
contract: Heat Death 704932 (SpellFamilyName 33) has one live effect: SPELL_AURA_ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER (107) with EffectMiscValue 1 (SPELLMOD_DURATION) and EffectBasePoints 14999 -> real 15000 ms, and EffectSpellClassMask word 3 bit 0x2 (2). Scanning Spell.dbc for the family-33 record whose own SpellFamilyFlags carry that exact bit finds Solar Eclipse's proc effect 704931 (SpellFamilyFlags_3 2, SpellName 'Solar Eclipse', Rank 'Proc'): effect 0 is SPELL_AURA_MOD_HIT_CHANCE (54) with EffectBasePoints -4 -> real -3, matching the tooltip's 'reduces the enemies chance to hit by 3%' on its own, independent of this talent. 704931 has no DurationIndex entry (falls back to SpellInfo::GetDuration() == 0, confirmed via SpellDuration.dbc), so without Heat Death the debuff is a 0 ms application; SPELLMOD_DURATION is read generically by Player::ApplySpellMod wherever a spell computes its own duration (Spell::CheckCast/Aura::CalcMaxDuration), so it needs no script -- it fires the moment a caster with 704932 has an aura computed for 704931. The 'spell_modifier' query metric calls exactly that native Player::ApplySpellMod(704931, SPELLMOD_DURATION, base) path directly, without casting anything or needing a proc chain (Solar Eclipse's own trigger plumbing, 704929/704930, is not part of this issue). Native handlers only; regression scenario for behaviour that already works.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Without Heat Death, Solar Eclipse's proc debuff keeps its shipped 0 ms duration
Heat Death extends the same debuff's duration to 15 seconds
